title: Right to Information Application Procedure under Section 6 of RTI Act 2005
content:
## 1. Application Submission
Under Section 6(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, any citizen of India may request information from a Public Authority.
- The request must be made in writing or through electronic means in English, Hindi, or in the official language of the area in which the application is being made.
- The applicant must specify the particulars of the information sought.
- The application must be accompanied by the prescribed application fee (₹10 for Central public authorities).

title: Right to Information Application Procedure under Section 6 of RTI Act 2005
content:
## 2. Addressee of Application
- The application should be addressed to the Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) or State Public Information Officer (SPIO) of the concerned department.
- If submitted to an Assistant Public Information Officer (APIO), an additional 5 days is added to the statutory response timeline.

title: Right to Information Application Procedure under Section 6 of RTI Act 2005
content:
## 3. Assistance to Citizens
Under Section 6(2), an applicant making request for information shall not be required to give any reason for requesting the information or any other personal details except those that may be necessary for contacting them.
Under Section 6(3), where an application is made to a public authority requesting information which is held by another public authority, the public authority shall transfer the application to that other public authority within 5 days from receipt and immediately inform the applicant.

title: Right to Information Application Procedure under Section 6 of RTI Act 2005
content:
## 4. Statutory Timelines
Under Section 7(1):
- General requests: Information must be provided or rejected within 30 days from the date of receipt.
- Life and Liberty: Where the information sought concerns the life or liberty of a person, it must be provided within 48 hours of receipt.
- Failure to give decision within 30 days is deemed a refusal under Section 7(2).

title: RTI First Appeal Procedure under Section 19 of RTI Act 2005
content:
## 1. Grounds for First Appeal
Under Section 19(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, any person who:
- Does not receive a decision within the specified 30 days time limit under Section 7(1), or
- Is aggrieved by a decision of the Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) or State Public Information Officer (SPIO) regarding rejection, incomplete information, or excessive fee demand,
may prefer a First Appeal.

title: RTI First Appeal Procedure under Section 19 of RTI Act 2005
content:
## 2. Limitation Period (Deadline)
- The appeal must be filed within 30 days from the expiry of the 30-day response period or within 30 days from the receipt of the PIO's decision.
- The First Appellate Authority (FAA) may admit the appeal after the expiry of 30 days if satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause.

title: RTI First Appeal Procedure under Section 19 of RTI Act 2005
content:
## 3. Appellate Authority
- The appeal is made to an officer senior in rank to the CPIO/SPIO in the same public authority (designated as the First Appellate Authority - FAA).
- There is no application fee for filing a First Appeal before Central Government authorities.

title: RTI First Appeal Procedure under Section 19 of RTI Act 2005
content:
## 4. Timelines for Disposal
Under Section 19(6):
- The appeal shall be disposed of within 30 days of receipt.
- In exceptional cases, for reasons to be recorded in writing, the disposal period may be extended up to a maximum of 45 days from the date of filing.
- If aggrieved by the FAA order, a Second Appeal lies to the Central Information Commission (CIC) or State Information Commission (SIC) within 90 days under Section 19(3).

title: Right to Information Rules 2012 - Fees, Formats and Payment Modes
content:
## 1. Application Fee
Under Rule 3 of the RTI Rules, 2012:
- An application for obtaining information under sub-section (1) of Section 6 shall be accompanied by a fee of ₹10 (Rupees Ten only).

title: Right to Information Rules 2012 - Fees, Formats and Payment Modes
content:
## 2. Permitted Modes of Payment
Under Rule 6, the fee can be paid by:
- Cash against proper official receipt.
- Demand Draft (DD) or Banker's Cheque drawn in favour of the Accounts Officer of the public authority.
- Indian Postal Order (IPO).
- Electronic payment via online portal (e.g. net banking, credit/debit card, UPI on rtionline.gov.in).

title: Right to Information Rules 2012 - Fees, Formats and Payment Modes
content:
## 3. Exemption for BPL Citizens
- No fee shall be charged from any person who belongs to Below Poverty Line (BPL) category, provided a copy of the BPL certificate issued by the appropriate Government is attached with the application.

title: Right to Information Rules 2012 - Fees, Formats and Payment Modes
content:
## 4. Format and Word Limit
Under Rule 3:
- An application shall not ordinarily exceed 500 words, excluding annexures containing addresses of other persons and documents.
- No application shall be rejected merely on the ground that it exceeds 500 words.

title: Right to Information Rules 2012 - Fees, Formats and Payment Modes
content:
## 5. Inspection and Copying Charges
Under Rule 4:
- ₹2 for each page (in A-4 or A-3 size paper) created or copied.
- Actual charge or cost price of a copy in larger size paper.
- Inspection of records: No fee for the first hour; and a fee of ₹5 for each subsequent hour (or fraction thereof).

title: Traffic e-Challan Citizen Dispute and Online Grievance Procedure
content:
## 1. Viewing and Verification of e-Challan
Citizens can check traffic violations and pending citations on the central MoRTH e-Challan portal (echallan.parivahan.gov.in) using:
- Challan Number, or
- Vehicle Registration Number (with last 5 digits of Chassis/Engine number), or
- Driving License Number.

title: Traffic e-Challan Citizen Dispute and Online Grievance Procedure
content:
## 2. Challenging an Incorrect or Wrongly Issued Challan
If an e-Challan is issued erroneously (e.g. cloned number plate, wrong vehicle photograph, camera calibration error, or emergency vehicle exemption):
1. Navigate to the "Complaint" / "Grievance" section on the e-Challan portal.
2. Enter the Challan Number, Vehicle Number, and citizen contact details.
3. Select the grievance category (e.g. "Wrong Vehicle Tagged", "Duplicate Payment", "Incorrect Violation Location").
4. Upload documentary evidence: photograph of the actual vehicle, Registration Certificate (RC), or GPS/toll logs proving the vehicle was elsewhere at the time of the violation.
5. The grievance is routed to the Traffic Police Enforcement Branch of the concerned district/commissionerate for verification.

title: Traffic e-Challan Citizen Dispute and Online Grievance Procedure
content:
## 3. Disputed Challans and Virtual Court Referral
- If the citizen contests the violation and refuses online compounding, the challan is marked as "Contested" and transferred to the Virtual Court / Judicial Magistrate having jurisdiction under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
- Citizens are issued a summon notice with a hearing date or can submit their defence online before the Virtual Court Magistrate.
- Paying the fine constitutes compounding the offense under Section 200 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, after which no further dispute can be entertained.

title: Telangana Traffic Police e-Challan Dispute Resolution and Compounding Rules
content:
## 1. e-Challan Payment Timelines
- Traffic e-challans issued by Telangana Police must be cleared within 60 days from the date of issue.
- Payment can be made online via Telangana Police e-Challan portal, MeeSeva centers, or Traffic Police Helpdesks.

title: Telangana Traffic Police e-Challan Dispute Resolution and Compounding Rules
content:
## 2. Challenging Erroneous Challans in Telangana
If a vehicle owner in Hyderabad / Telangana receives an erroneous e-challan:
1. Citizen can raise an online dispute through the "Report / Grievance" link on echallan.tspolice.gov.in.
2. Submit vehicle RC copy, challan number, and photographic evidence demonstrating discrepancies in vehicle make, color, or registration number plate.
3. Citizens can also approach the Traffic Police Help Desk at the Commissionerate (e.g. Traffic Complex, Goshamahal, Hyderabad or Gachibowli, Cyberabad) in person.
4. If verified that the challan was caused by automated ANPR camera error or number plate masking by another vehicle, the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP - Traffic) cancels the challan.

title: Telangana Traffic Police e-Challan Dispute Resolution and Compounding Rules
content:
## 3. Lok Adalat Dispute Settlement
- Pending disputed traffic challans can be contested or compounded with statutory fee waivers during quarterly National Lok Adalat sittings organized by the Telangana State Legal Services Authority (TSLSA).
- Notice of Lok Adalat dates is published on the official police portal.

title: TSSPDCL Consumer Complaint and Billing Dispute Resolution Procedure
content:
## 1. Disputed Bill Submission
When a consumer receives an inflated electricity bill, unexpected arrears demand, or disputed tariff classification from TSSPDCL:
- The consumer must file a formal complaint in writing or through the TSSPDCL mobile app / web portal before the Assistant Engineer (AE - Operations) or Section Officer having jurisdiction.
- Quote the unique Consumer Service Connection Number (USC Number), consumer name, billing month, and clear grounds of dispute (e.g. meter reading error, stuck meter, wrong category).

title: TSSPDCL Consumer Complaint and Billing Dispute Resolution Procedure
content:
## 2. Provisional Payment Requirement During Dispute
- Under TSERC Consumer Service Regulations, filing a complaint does not grant automatic stay of disconnection.
- To prevent disconnection during the investigation, the consumer is generally required to pay an amount equal to the average of the previous three undisputed months' consumption, pending final dispute resolution.

title: TSSPDCL Consumer Complaint and Billing Dispute Resolution Procedure
content:
## 3. Rectification and Refund Procedure
- TSSPDCL staff must inspect the meter and verify billing records within 7 days of complaint registration.
- If billing error or meter defect is established, revised bill with credit adjustment is issued in the immediate subsequent billing cycle.
- If the Section Officer fails to resolve the dispute within 15 days, the consumer may escalate the complaint to the Divisional Engineer (DE) or the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF).

title: TSERC Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF) and Ombudsman Regulations
content:
## 1. Establishment and Jurisdiction of CGRF
Every distribution licensee in Telangana (TSSPDCL and TSNPDCL) maintains a Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF) comprising a Chairperson and Technical/Independent members.
- CGRF has jurisdiction over complaints relating to billing disputes, delay in power supply restoration, meter inaccuracies, and deficiency of service.
- The Forum does NOT entertain matters pending before courts, assessment of unauthorized use under Section 126, or theft under Section 135 of Electricity Act 2003.

title: TSERC Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF) and Ombudsman Regulations
content:
## 2. Procedure for Filing Grievance before CGRF
1. A consumer aggrieved by non-resolution by DISCOM internal officers may file a petition before CGRF in the prescribed Form.
2. Provide copy of original complaint, DISCOM reply (if any), consumer service connection number, and supporting documents.
3. No fee is payable for filing a grievance before CGRF.
4. CGRF provides acknowledgment within 3 days and conducts hearings.

title: TSERC Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF) and Ombudsman Regulations
content:
## 3. Disposal Timeline
- CGRF must pass a reasoned final order within 45 days from the date of receipt of the grievance.
- The licensee (DISCOM) must implement the CGRF order within the timeframe specified in the order (typically 15 to 30 days).

title: TSERC Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF) and Ombudsman Regulations
content:
## 4. Representation to Electricity Ombudsman
- Any consumer aggrieved by non-redressal of grievance by CGRF or non-implementation of CGRF order by DISCOM may submit a representation to the Electricity Ombudsman.
- Limitation: The appeal to the Ombudsman must be preferred within 30 days from the date of receipt of CGRF order.

title: Electricity Disconnection Notice Requirements under Section 56 of Electricity Act 2003
content:
## 1. Mandatory Disconnection Notice Period
Under Section 56(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003:
- Where any person neglects to pay any charge for electricity or any sum other than a charge for electricity due from him, the licensee may cut off the supply of electricity.
- MANDATORY REQUIREMENT: The licensee must give NOT LESS THAN 15 CLEAR DAYS' NOTICE IN WRITING to the consumer before disconnecting supply.
- Disconnection without serving the statutory 15 days' written notice is illegal and violates Section 56.

title: Electricity Disconnection Notice Requirements under Section 56 of Electricity Act 2003
content:
## 2. Recovery Limitation
Under Section 56(2):
- Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, no sum due from any consumer shall be recoverable after a period of 2 years from the date when such sum became first due, unless such sum has been shown continuously as recoverable as arrear of charges for electricity supplied.
- Licensee shall not cut off supply if the sum became due more than 2 years ago and was not continuously shown as pending arrear.

title: Electricity Disconnection Notice Requirements under Section 56 of Electricity Act 2003
content:
## 3. Immediate Reconnection on Payment
- Upon payment of the outstanding undisputed charges along with prescribed reconnection fee, the licensee is statutorily required to reconnect supply within 24 hours in urban areas (48 hours in rural areas).

title: GHMC Property Tax Assessment Objection and Revision Petition under Section 282
content:
## 1. Statutory Right to File Revision Petition
Under Section 282 of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) Act, 1955:
- Any property owner or taxpayer aggrieved by a new property tax assessment, enhanced annual rental value (ARV), or a Special Notice of property tax demand has the statutory right to file a Revision Petition (Objection Petition).

title: GHMC Property Tax Assessment Objection and Revision Petition under Section 282
content:
## 2. Limitation Period (Deadline)
- The Revision Petition must be filed within 30 days from the date of service of the Special Notice or bill of demand.
- Petitions filed after 30 days are liable to be dismissed as time-barred unless condoned for sufficient recorded reasons.

title: GHMC Property Tax Assessment Objection and Revision Petition under Section 282
content:
## 3. Grounds for Objection
A revision petition may challenge the assessment on grounds including:
- Inaccurate plinth / built-up area measurement.
- Erroneous classification of property usage (e.g. assessing residential premises as commercial).
- Incorrect zone or sub-zone categorization for Monthly Rental Value (MRV).
- Disregard of statutory age depreciation for older buildings.
- Vacancy remission claim where premises remained unoccupied.

title: GHMC Property Tax Assessment Objection and Revision Petition under Section 282
content:
## 4. Documents to Submit
- Copy of GHMC Special Notice / Property Tax Assessment Notice.
- Registered Sale Deed or Title Deed copy proving ownership.
- Sanctioned building plan or architect plinth area measurement certificate.
- Electricity bill and property tax receipts for previous years.
- Photographs of property showing current actual usage.

title: GHMC Property Tax Assessment Objection and Revision Petition under Section 282
content:
## 5. Disposal and Hearing
- The Deputy Commissioner / Assessment Authority must issue a notice of hearing giving the taxpayer an opportunity to be heard in person or via authorized representative.
- A reasoned written order reducing, confirming, or revising the assessment must be passed.

title: GHMC Property Tax Appeal Procedure to Civil Court under Section 286
content:
## 1. Appeal before the Chief Judge, City Civil Court
Under Section 286 of the GHMC Act, 1955:
- An appeal against any order passed by the Deputy Commissioner upon a revision petition under Section 282 lies to the Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad.

title: GHMC Property Tax Appeal Procedure to Civil Court under Section 286
content:
## 2. Pre-conditions for Filing Appeal
- The appeal must be presented within 30 days from the date of the order disposing of the revision petition.
- Pre-requisite condition: The appellant must have first filed a revision petition under Section 282 and had it decided by the municipal authority. An appeal cannot be made directly without exhausting the Section 282 revision remedy.
- Statutory Pre-deposit: The taxpayer must deposit with the Commissioner the undisputed tax amount or the percentage prescribed under the Act pending the appeal.

title: GHMC Property Tax Appeal Procedure to Civil Court under Section 286
content:
## 3. High Court Remedy
- If either party is aggrieved by the judgment of the Chief Judge, City Civil Court under Section 286, an appeal or revision lies to the High Court for the State of Telangana on questions of law.

title: National Food Security Act 2013 - Chapter VII Grievance Redressal and Appeal Procedure
content:
## 1. Statutory Grievance Redressal Mechanism
Under Chapter VII of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013:
- Section 14 mandates an internal grievance redressal mechanism (toll-free helpline, citizen service portals) for each State Food and Civil Supplies Department.
- Section 15 mandates the appointment of a District Grievance Redressal Officer (DGRO) for each district to hear complaints regarding non-issuance, arbitrary cancellation, or wrongful rejection of ration cards and subsidized foodgrains.

title: National Food Security Act 2013 - Chapter VII Grievance Redressal and Appeal Procedure
content:
## 2. Challenging Ration Card Rejection or Ineligibility Intimation
If an applicant receives an intimation rejecting an NFSA Food Security Card (Ration Card) or pension benefits:
1. File an application/appeal before the District Grievance Redressal Officer (usually the District Supply Officer or Joint Collector) within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice.
2. Specify the erroneous rejection grounds (e.g. wrongful presumption of landholding, faulty exclusion criteria, income certificate discrepancies, or Aadhaar mismatch).
3. Attach supporting evidence: family income certificate issued by Tahsildar, residential proof, Aadhaar cards of all family members, and electricity bill showing domestic connection within quota.

title: National Food Security Act 2013 - Chapter VII Grievance Redressal and Appeal Procedure
content:
## 3. Hearing and Disposal by DGRO
- The DGRO conducts summary inquiry, summons records from the local Tahsildar / Mandal Revenue Officer (MRO), and passes written disposal orders within 30 days.
- If aggrieved by the DGRO order, an appeal lies to the State Food Commission under Section 16 within 30 days.

title: Telangana Aasara Social Security Pension Ineligibility and Appeal Guidelines
content:
## 1. Scope of Aasara Pension Scheme
The Telangana Government provides monthly social security pensions under the "Aasara" scheme to Old Age Pensioners (OAP), Widows, Disabled Persons (TOD), Weavers, and Toddy Tappers meeting designated socio-economic criteria.

title: Telangana Aasara Social Security Pension Ineligibility and Appeal Guidelines
content:
## 2. Ineligibility Notices and Rejection Grounds
Applications for Aasara pension or existing beneficiaries may receive rejection/disqualification notices citing exclusion criteria:
- Ownership of large agricultural land (exceeding 3 acres wetland or 7.5 acres dryland).
- Presence of an earning government or formal private sector employee in the family.
- Ownership of four-wheeler vehicle (excluding one commercial taxi/auto).
- Annual family income exceeding rural/urban poverty limits as per civil supplies records.

title: Telangana Aasara Social Security Pension Ineligibility and Appeal Guidelines
content:
## 3. Appeal Procedure for Rejected Applicants
If an eligible applicant is wrongly rejected or their pension is suspended:
1. File an appeal representation before the Project Director, District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) or District Collector.
2. In urban municipal areas, submit the appeal through the Municipal Commissioner / Ward Office.
3. Submit within 30 days from the date of the rejection notice.
4. Attach mandatory certificates:
   - Gram Sabha / Ward verification certificate of vulnerability.
   - Non-ownership certificate from Mandal Revenue Officer (MRO) for disputed land/vehicles.
   - Medical Board (SADAREM) disability certificate (for disability pension claims).
   - Age verification proof (Aadhaar / Voter ID / Birth certificate).
5. The District Collectorate conducts re-verification and issues an inclusion order if eligibility criteria are fulfilled.
